title: COMIC: Reference-Aware Safety Gating for Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.17234v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are increasingly used to interact with screenshots, scanned documents, diagrams, and other visually grounded inputs. This shift introduces a new safety risk: in many multimodal jailbreaks, neither the prompt nor the image is harmful in isolation. Unsafe behavior emerges only when the model binds an apparently benign operation, such as summarizing, translating, or following, to a localized visual target. This reveals a structural weakness in current multimodal defenses, which largely moderate the prompt-image pair as a whole even though the true security-relevant unit is the grounded operation-target pair produced during dereference. In this work, we identify and analyze this reference-dependent failure mode and show that existing defenses degrade when harmful semantics are localized, activated only after grounding, and dependent on visual reference resolution. translated_title: COMIC：面向多模态大语言模型的参考感知安全门控机制
translated_abstract: 多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）越来越多地被用于与截图、扫描文档、图表及其他视觉基础输入进行交互。这种转变引入了新的安全风险：在许多多模态越狱攻击中，提示词或图像单独来看均无害，但只有当模型将看似良性的操作（如总结、翻译或跟随）绑定到局部视觉目标时，不安全行为才会出现。这揭示了当前多模态防御机制中的结构性弱点：这些防御大多将提示-图像对作为一个整体进行审核，而真正的安全相关单元是在解引用过程中产生的“接地操作-目标对”。在本工作中，我们识别并分析了这种依赖参考的失败模式，并表明当有害语义被局部化、仅在接地后激活且依赖于视觉参考解析时，现有防御会退化。为解决此问题，我们提出了COMIC机制。
tldr: 本文首次识别了多模态大语言模型中依赖视觉参考的越狱攻击模式，并提出了一种参考感知的安全门控机制，以针对局部化有害语义的接地操作进行防御。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies a reference-dependent jailbreak failure mode in multimodal large language models and proposes a reference-aware safety gating mechanism to defend against localized harmful semantics in grounded operations.
